INTRO.text: Welcome to the System Wizard demo. This tool lets you describe a goal in plain language, then generates and iteratively fixes a shell script to accomplish it. Let's walk through the full workflow.

HUB_OVERVIEW.text: This is the Cognotik App Hub. Let's launch the System Wizard application.

LOGIN_PROMPT.text: We need to log in first to access the applications.

LOGIN_SUCCESS.text: Logged in successfully. Now we can see all available applications in the hub.

APP_OPENED.text: The System Wizard is now open. We can see the Goal tab where we describe what we want to accomplish.

GOAL_TAB.text: Let's start by defining our goal. We'll describe what we want the shell script to do in plain language.

GOAL_TIPS.text: Notice the tips section below. Being specific about file paths, outputs, and constraints helps the AI generate a better script.

GOAL_TYPING.text: We'll type a goal that asks the wizard to gather system information and write a summary report.

GOAL_SAVED.text: The goal has been saved. Now let's move to the Pipeline tab to generate and run our script.

PIPELINE_TAB.text: Here's the Pipeline tab. It shows a visual diagram of the three stages: Goal, Generate, and Run and Fix. Each stage updates its status as we progress.

PIPELINE_OVERVIEW.text: The pipeline has two main steps. First, the AI generates a shell script from our goal. Then it runs the script and automatically fixes any errors.

SETTINGS_TAB.text: Before running the pipeline, let's configure the AI models in the Settings tab.

SETTINGS_MODELS.text: We need to select both a Smart Model for script generation and a Fast Model for parsing and quick tasks. Both are required.

SETTINGS_SAVED.text: Model settings have been saved. Now let's go back to the Pipeline and run it.

SETTINGS_SKIPPED.text: We'll skip the settings configuration for now and use the previously saved model selections.

CODEGEN_INTRO.text: Step one is script generation. The AI reads our goal and writes a shell script to accomplish it. Let's click Generate.

CODEGEN_STARTED.text: The AI is now generating the shell script. We can monitor the session in real time via the provided link.

CODEGEN_DONE.text: The script has been generated successfully. Let's review what the AI wrote.

CODEGEN_SKIPPED.text: We'll skip individual script generation and use the full pipeline run instead.

MANUAL_MODE_INTRO.text: Alternatively, you can switch to Paste and Edit mode to write or paste your own script instead of using AI generation.

MANUAL_MODE_SKIPPED.text: We'll skip the manual editing mode for this demo and let the AI generate the script.

RUN_FIX_INTRO.text: Step two is Run and Auto-Fix. The script is executed, and if any errors occur, the AI automatically fixes them in a loop until it succeeds.

RUN_FIX_STARTED.text: The script is now running. If it encounters any errors, the auto-fix system will attempt to repair and re-run it.

RUN_FIX_DONE.text: Execution is complete. The script ran successfully. Let's check the results.

RUN_FIX_SKIPPED.text: We'll skip the individual run step and use the full pipeline instead.

FULL_PIPELINE_INTRO.text: Instead of running each step individually, we can use the Run Entire Pipeline button. This saves the goal, generates the script, and runs it with auto-fix — all in one click.

FULL_PIPELINE_STARTED.text: The full pipeline is now running. The batch log below shows progress for each stage.

FULL_PIPELINE_DONE.text: The entire pipeline has completed successfully. All stages show a green checkmark.

FULL_PIPELINE_SKIPPED.text: We'll skip the full pipeline run since we already ran the steps individually.

PLATFORM_TOGGLE.text: Notice the platform toggle at the top. You can switch between Shell for Linux and macOS, or Windows for PowerShell scripts.

RESULTS_TAB.text: Let's switch to the Results tab to review everything that was generated.

RESULTS_SCRIPT.text: Here's the generated shell script. We can copy it to the clipboard or download it directly.

RESULTS_LOG.text: The Execution Log tab shows the full run and fix log, rendered as formatted Markdown. This includes any auto-fix attempts that were made.

RESULTS_GOAL.text: And here's our original goal for reference, exactly as we typed it.

USAGE_TAB.text: The Usage tab tracks API token usage and estimated costs for this session. It shows prompt tokens, completion tokens, and a per-model breakdown.

USAGE_SKIPPED.text: We'll skip the usage details for this demo.

EXAMPLE_PROMPTS.text: The Goal tab also includes example prompts. Let's try one to see how it works.

EXAMPLE_PROMPTS_SKIPPED.text: We'll skip the example prompts and write our own goal instead.

OUTRO.text: And that's the complete workflow of the System Wizard! You describe a goal, the AI writes a script, and it runs and fixes itself automatically. Thank you for watching!
